metadata.case_name: LEUNG YUNG CHEUNG v. FLY KING TRANSPORTATION CO LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: warehouseman; promoted to team leader on 1 Oct 2013
plaintiff.education_level: No formal education in China; cannot read or write Chinese except signing his name; illiterate

injuries.description: soft tissue injuries to both ankles
source: I find that plaintiff suffered only from injuries to his ankles in the alleged accident due to defendant’s breaches of duties (i.e. he was only hit on his right ankle by the 5th plank and his left ankle got injured by skidding and falling into the 1st gap).

On the common opinion by Dr Fu & Dr Ho on this point in the joint report, and on the same diagnosis of NLCHC, I find that plaintiff suffered only “soft tissue” injuries to “both ankles” in the alleged accident as a result of defendant’s breaches of its duties.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of ankle, unspecified

injuries.description: partial tear in anterior cruciate ligament and tear of medial meniscus of right knee (shown on MRI scan)
source: the partial tear in anterior cruciate ligament and tear of medial meniscus of right knee suffered by plaintiff (and shown on MRI scan)
injuries.icd_description: Injury to multiple structures of knee

manifestations.description: stiffness and weakness of right ankle
occasional left ankle pain and weakness
right lower limb weakness requiring use of a stick

treatments_received.treatment: Accident & Emergency attendance at North Lantau Hospital (NLH) on 10 Oct 2013
source: On 10 Oct 2013 i.e. 2 days later, at about 1100 hours, the plaintiff attended Accident & Emergency Department (A&E) of North Lantau Hospital (NLH).

treatments_received.treatment: Re-attendance at A&E of NLH (67 occasions between 13 Oct 2013 and 8 Sept 2014)
source: Between 13 Oct 2013 and 8 Sept 2014, the plaintiff re-attended A&E of NLH on another 67 occasions.

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at North Lantau Community Health Centre (NLCHC) from 2 Nov 2013 to 1 Aug 2014
source: On 2 Nov 2013, he first attended North Lantau Community Health Centre (NLCHC). He attended NLCHC thereafter from time to time until 1 Aug 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy (9 sessions at NLH between 25 Feb 2014 and 10 Jun 2014)
source: He had 9 sessions of physiotherapy at NLH between 25 Feb 2014 and 10 Jun 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: Occupational therapy at NLH (2 May 2014 to 29 Sept 2014)
source: And he received occupational therapy at NLH from 2 May 2014 to 29 Sept 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: MRI scan of right ankle and right knee in China on 25 Jul 2014
source: On 25 July 2014, the plaintiff received MRI scan over his right ankle and right knee in China.

treatments_received.treatment: Private MRI scan of right ankle and knee in Hong Kong on 10 Apr 2015
source: On 10 Apr 2015, private MRI scan of plaintiff’s right ankle and knee were performed in Hong Kong.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultations with private orthopaedic specialist Dr Lau (from 7 Oct 2014; no less than 19 consultations up to 22 Sep 2015)
source: Starting from 7 Oct 2014, he started consulting a private orthopedic specialist, Dr Lau Sing Ki Kentric (Dr Lau). No less than 19 consultations to Dr Lau were made by him up to 22 Sep 2015.

treatments_received.treatment: Referral and consultations at Department of Orthopedics and Traumatology (O&T), Princess Margaret Hospital (first appointment 24 Feb 2015; last seen 30 Jun 2015)
source: The plaintiff was also referred to Department of Orthopedics and Traumatology (O&T) of Princess Margaret Hospital (PMH). He had his first appointment there on 24 Feb 2015. He was last seen for follow-up on 30 Jun 2015.

treatments_received.treatment: Bonesetter consultations (江氏祖傳骨科跌打醫館 and 祿盛堂陳昭烱骨傷科)
source: Mr Gidwani finally in his oral address agreed with the 2 sums of $15,460 and $400 for bonesetters ...
for 江氏祖傳骨科跌打醫館

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies

losses.description: Cannot return to his pre-accident job as he can no longer stand for long or push heavy objects as he used to
